data.title: MDQ Specification Audit: fill-in
data.scope: The fill-in question type: `docs/question-types/fill-in.md` and `schema/fill-in.yaml`, read against `docs/references/grammar.md`, `docs/references/patterns.md`, `docs/question-types/question-base.md`, `docs/exam.md` and `docs/responses.md`. The blanks reuse the short-answer, numeric and choice rules; earlier audits already settled those rules.

data.title: Contradictions
Ambiguities
Omissions
Inconsistencies
Grammar violations
Schema mismatches

data.methodology:
The audit script `scripts/spec_audit.py` passed all 15 steps before the audit started: it compiles every Lark snippet, checks the Additional Rules tables against `docs/lint-codes.md` and the corpus, and checks the frontmatter tables against the schemas.

The lead auditor read `docs/question-types/fill-in.md` with the shared specs and recorded contradictions, ambiguities, omissions and inconsistencies. The audit focused on what is specific to fill-in: the blank references, the choice blanks, the frontmatter maps keyed by blank id, the grading strategies and the response shape. The blank rules that fill-in reuses from short-answer and numeric were checked for agreement with the decisions of the earlier audits.

One subagent turned the fill-in grammar and the shared grammar into Lark and tested what they accept and reject. A second, independent subagent scanned the fill-in document and schema, ran each complete example through `mdq validate`, and checked the Additional Rules table against the MUST, SHOULD and MAY requirements of the text.

data.title: Prose allows two behaviors for a misplaced blank; the rules table and the corpus require specific codes
data.snippet:
illegal. A `[^slug]` found in any of them is not a blank: implementations MUST
either reject the document or leave the text exactly as written, and MUST NOT
silently drop it.
data.description: The prose lets an implementation either reject a `[^slug]` in a heading, list item, table cell, blockquote or fenced code, or keep it as text. The Additional Rules table has one rule, `misplaced-blank` (error) for 'blanks may only appear in a plain text run of a paragraph'. The corpus uses three different outcomes: a heading gives `unreferenced-blank` (`examples/invalid/fill-in-misplaced-blank-heading`), a code span gives `misplaced-blank` (`examples/invalid/fill-in-misplaced-blank-code-span`), and fenced code is valid text (`examples/valid/fill-in/blank-in-code-is-text`). Nothing in the spec says which block kind gives which outcome. Lines 174-176 also put inline code with link text and emphasis, but a code span is literal text in CommonMark, as fenced code is.
data.impact: Two conforming implementations can give different lint codes, or one accepts a document the other rejects. The corpus fixes behavior that the spec does not state.
data.fix: Give one outcome per context in a table: for example, fenced code, indented code and code spans are literal text; a `[^slug]` in a heading, list item, table cell or blockquote of the stem, or inside emphasis or link text, is `misplaced-blank`. Remove 'either ... or'.
data.conditions: A `[^slug]` in a heading, list item, table cell, blockquote, code span or emphasis of the stem.

data.title: The spec does not say which paragraphs form the stem, so blanks in two paragraphs fail
data.snippet:
stem  : inline_md? (blank inline_md?)+
blank : "[^" SLUG "]"
data.description:
The stem grammar describes one run of inline content. The text never says where the preamble ends and the stem begins, or whether the stem can have more than one paragraph with blanks. `docs/question-types/question-base.md:132-134` only says implementations SHOULD require a one-paragraph stem. With the reference implementation, the document 'Intro.

First [^a] paragraph.

Middle.

Second [^b] paragraph.

[^a/short-answer]: x

[^b/short-answer]: y' fails with `unreferenced-blank` for `a`: the first paragraph with a blank goes to the preamble, where line 178 says a `[^slug]` is literal text. The spec does not exercise this case and does not say it is an error.
data.impact: Authors write cloze texts that span paragraphs. The result is an error that names the wrong cause, and another implementation can accept the same document.
data.fix: State the rule: either the stem is the last paragraph before the definitions (and a `[^slug]` in an earlier paragraph gives a specific error), or the stem is every block from the first paragraph with a blank to the definitions. Add an example to the corpus.
data.conditions: Blanks in two or more paragraphs.

data.title: The spec does not say whether blank definitions must be contiguous
data.snippet:
Definitions may appear in any order, and that order need not match the order
the stem references them.
data.description: The text allows any order but does not say if a paragraph can stand between two definitions. In the reference implementation, a paragraph after the first definition ends the body: a later `[^b/short-answer]: y` goes to the epilogue as text, and the stem reference `[^b]` gives `undefined-blank`, which names the wrong cause.
data.impact: An author who puts an explanation between definitions gets an error that points at the stem, not at the definition.
data.fix: State that the definitions form one sequence of blocks, separated only by blank lines, and that the first other block starts the epilogue. Consider a dedicated lint for a definition tag in the epilogue.
data.conditions: A paragraph between two blank definitions.

data.title: Under no-mistakes and all-or-nothing, the multiple choice strategy for a choice blank is not stated
data.snippet:
* A **choice blank** is graded like a
  [multiple choice](multiple-choice.md#grading) question, under the strategy
  the fill-in question declares.
data.description: Multiple choice accepts only `partial` and `symmetric` (`docs/exam.md:357-358`). The fill-in question can declare `no-mistakes` or `all-or-nothing`, which a multiple choice question does not accept, so 'under the strategy the fill-in question declares' has no meaning for these two. Lines 453-456 imply the answer only through an example ('Under `partial`, `no-mistakes` and `all-or-nothing` that same wrong pick scores 0').
data.impact: An implementation can raise an error, or score the blank with `symmetric`, for a fill-in under `no-mistakes`.
data.fix: Add a mapping: a choice blank is scored with multiple choice `partial` under `partial`, `no-mistakes` and `all-or-nothing`, and with `symmetric` under `symmetric`, as in the exam table at `docs/exam.md:346-351`.

data.title: An empty blank in the response is not defined
data.snippet: A blank the student left empty scores 0 under every strategy.
data.description: `docs/responses.md:213-231` does not say how a response marks an empty blank: a missing key, a `null` value, or both. For a short answer blank, `""` is not empty: `docs/responses.md:200-204` says it is graded like any other text. The spec also does not say what an empty mapping `{}` is (all blanks empty, or a skip like `null`), nor whether a value of the wrong type for a blank (a number for a choice blank, a list for a short answer blank) is a `ResponseError`.
data.impact: The strategies `no-mistakes` and `all-or-nothing` treat an empty blank differently from a wrong one, so the score depends on a rule the spec does not give.
data.fix: In `docs/responses.md`, Fill in the blanks: a missing key and a `null` value are an empty blank; `{}` is a response with every blank empty (the question is not skipped); a value of the wrong type is a malformed response by the rule of the blank's type. Add response cases to the grading corpus.

data.title: A blank referenced more than once in the stem has no rule
data.snippet:
Every blank referenced by the stem MUST be defined, and every definition MUST
be referenced by the stem.
data.description: Nothing says whether the stem can reference the same id twice, as in 'The capital is [^c]. Write [^c] again.'. The response has one value per id, so two inputs would share one answer.
data.impact: An implementation can render two inputs bound to one key, render one, or reject the document.
data.fix: State that each blank id appears at most once in the stem, with an error code (for example `duplicate-blank-reference`), or state that repeated references share one input.

data.title: Several Markdown parse errors of blank definitions are only in the corpus
data.snippet: | blanks[]             | error    | parse-error        | a short answer blank defines each block at most once[^5]           |
data.description: The corpus gives `parse-error` for cases the Additional Rules table does not list and the text does not settle: a blank line between `[^bioma]:` and its choice list (`examples/invalid/fill-in-blank-line-before-choices`; line 226 says 'must start on the following line' but gives no code), an unknown kind suffix such as `[^resposta/essay]:` (`fill-in-unknown-blank-kind`), two choice definitions for one id (`fill-in-two-choice-definitions`) and one id with two kinds (`fill-in-two-kinds-one-blank`). Text on the tag line of a choice definition (`[^capital]: Brasília`) has no stated outcome. The table also omits the rule of line 319-321 that a list item right after the content of a short answer definition is a `parse-error`; the short answer table has it (`docs/question-types/short-answer.md:511`).
data.impact: An implementation that reads only the spec can accept these documents or report other codes.
data.fix: Add a rule per case to the table: blank line before the choice list, text on a choice tag line, unknown kind suffix, a second definition of an id (any kind), and a list item right after short answer content.

data.title: The Blank schema says a bare tag infers its kind from what follows
data.snippet:
required here even though the surface syntax may leave it implicit
      (`[^capital]:` infers its kind from the definition that follows,
      while `[^size/numeric]:` states it).
data.description: `docs/question-types/fill-in.md:203` says a bare `[^slug]:` is always a choice blank. The kind is not inferred from the definition.
data.impact: A reader of the schema can expect `[^capital]: Brasília` to be a short answer blank.
data.fix: Write: '`[^capital]:` is a choice blank, while `[^size/numeric]:` and `[^city/short-answer]:` state their kind.'

data.title: The ShortAnswerBlank description lists answer forms that no longer exist
data.snippet:
exactly like a short-answer question. Carries the same answer
      machinery: a list of accepted responses, a regular expression, or
      `accept`/`reject` pattern lists that can attach feedback.
data.description: A short answer blank has only the `accept`/`reject` pattern lists (and `preAccept`/`preReject`); a regex is one form of pattern, not a separate field. The description of `accept` (line 140) also cites only the alias `[^id/short-answer/accept]`, not the main tag `[^id/short-answer]`.
data.impact: Misleads readers of the schema about the fields of the blank.
data.fix: Write: 'Carries the same answer machinery: `accept` and `reject` pattern lists, which can attach feedback.' In `accept`, cite `[^id/short-answer]` (alias `[^id/short-answer/accept]`).

data.title: A choice blank has three names: choice blank, multiple choice blank and type multiple-choice
data.snippet:
## Multiple choice blanks

Multiple-choice blanks are represented by a reference definition followed by a
data.description: The rules table, the Feedback and the Grading sections say 'choice blank'; the section heading and its anchor say 'Multiple choice blanks'; the JSON `type` is `multiple-choice`. The other two kinds use one term each (numeric blank, short answer blank).
data.impact: Minor: readers must map three terms to one concept.
data.fix: Use 'choice blank' in prose and headings, and state once that its JSON `type` is `multiple-choice`.

data.title: For a pending fill-in, the spec does not say what score the instructor supplies
data.snippet:
A response to
the question is settled only when the response to every blank is settled; if
a blank leaves its response to the instructor, the whole question is pending.
data.description: `docs/responses.md` (Pending) says a pending response has no score until the instructor supplies one. For a fill-in, the instructor can score the pending blank (then the strategy combines it with the other blanks) or the whole question (then the strategy is bypassed). The range of a blank score from the instructor (only 0 or 1, as in a short answer blank, or any value in [0, 1]) is also not stated.
data.impact: An LMS cannot tell which value to ask the instructor for, and `no-mistakes` gives different results for a blank score of 0.5.
data.fix: State that the instructor scores each pending blank, in [0, 1], and that the strategy then combines the blank scores as usual.

data.text: The worked grading table covers all four strategies with empty, wrong, partial-credit and negative blank scores, and the values agree with the formulas.

The frontmatter maps (`preAccept`, `preReject`, `incorrectFeedback`, `domain`, `decimalPlaces`) each show the Markdown form and the JSON form, and the rules table gives the same two codes for each: `undefined-blank` for an unknown id and `schema-error` for a blank of the wrong kind.
The numeric blank rules defer to the numeric question for domain, decimal places, exact arithmetic, units and valid responses, without restating them, so the two cannot drift.

data.title: The spec does not say which paragraph is the stem when several paragraphs hold blanks
data.snippet: A blank may appear **only in a regular paragraph, in a run of plain text**.
data.description: Line 152 says a blank may appear in any regular paragraph, but line 178 says only the stem holds blanks, and the stem grammar (line 141) is one inline sequence. The spec never says which block is the stem when the introduction has several paragraphs (the last paragraph before the first definition?), nor whether a stem may span several paragraphs. The reference implementation treats only the last paragraph as the stem: in `The capital of Brazil is [^capital].` followed by a second paragraph `Its largest city is [^city].`, `[^capital]` becomes literal preamble text and the document fails with `unreferenced-blank`.
data.impact: Authors who split a fill-in text into two paragraphs get a confusing unreferenced-blank error, and a second implementation can reasonably accept the document. The two would disagree on validity.
data.fix: State that the stem is the last paragraph before the first blank definition (or allow a multi-paragraph stem), state what happens to `[^id]` in an earlier paragraph, and add an example.
data.conditions: A fill-in question whose blanks are spread across two or more paragraphs.

data.title: A `[^slug]` in a heading, list item, table cell or blockquote may be either an error or literal text
data.snippet: either reject the document or leave the text exactly as written, and MUST NOT
data.description: The spec lets each implementation choose between rejecting the document and keeping the marker as text. The choice changes validity: mdq-py accepts `## Footnotes look like [^note]` (no definition of `note`) as preamble text, and also a list item `* A marker like [^note] here.`, while an implementation that picks the other option rejects the same document. In the stem, a blank inside a list item gets `misplaced-blank` from mdq-py, and in a heading `unreferenced-blank` (examples/invalid/fill-in-misplaced-blank-heading.lint.json), so even the lint codes differ by block kind.
data.impact: The same document is valid in one conformant implementation and invalid in another.
data.fix: Pick one behavior per block kind and the lint code for it (for example: literal text outside the stem paragraph, `misplaced-blank` inside it), and add it to the Additional Rules table.

data.title: A marker in a code span is an error in the stem but literal text in fenced code and in the epilogue
data.snippet:
The same reasoning rules out link text, image alt text, emphasis and inline
code: a blank must be a direct child of the paragraph, with only plain text
data.description: Line 159-160 says a blank inside fenced code is literal text, because code is literal. The same argument applies to a code span, yet a code span in the stem is `misplaced-blank` (examples/invalid/fill-in-misplaced-blank-code-span), while a code span in the epilogue is literal text (examples/valid/fill-in/blank-in-code-is-text). An author who wants to show the syntax `[^capital]` in the stem cannot.
data.impact: Inconsistent rule; a stem cannot quote the blank syntax in code.
data.fix: Either treat a code span in the stem as literal text like fenced code, or explain why inline code differs.

data.title: The spec does not say if the stem may reference the same blank twice
data.snippet: Every blank referenced by the stem MUST be defined, and every definition MUST
data.description: Nothing allows or forbids `The [^x] river meets the [^x] river.` mdq-py accepts it. The response is a mapping from blank id to one response (responses.md, Fill in the blanks), so the two markers would have to share one input, and the spec does not say how a renderer shows it or how many blank scores the grading mean counts. No example exercises it.
data.impact: Implementations and renderers can disagree on validity, rendering and grading weight.
data.fix: Forbid a repeated reference with a lint code, or define that all markers of one id share one response and count once.
data.conditions: A stem that references one blank id more than once.

data.title: The spec does not say where the blank definitions end and the epilogue starts
data.snippet:
Definitions may appear in any order, and that order need not match the order
the stem references them. The `blanks` array preserves the order the
data.description: The spec never says whether other blocks may appear between definitions. mdq-py ends the body at the first non-definition block: a paragraph `Some note.` between `[^a/short-answer]` and `[^b/short-answer]` gives `undefined-blank` for `b`, with no hint that the paragraph is the cause. examples/valid/fill-in/epilogue-nested-list shows an epilogue after the definitions, but no rule is written.
data.impact: Authors get a misleading error, and implementations can choose different boundaries.
data.fix: State that the body is the contiguous run of definitions and that the first other block starts the epilogue (or allow interleaving), and give the diagnostic for a definition in the epilogue.
data.conditions: A paragraph or other block between two blank definitions.

data.title: A short answer blank with only a reject block is not addressed, unlike a short answer question that MUST have an accept block
data.snippet: A short answer blank has the two blocks of a short answer question:
data.description: short-answer.md line 140 says a question MUST have a `[short-answer]` block. The fill-in grammar `short_answer_def : accept_def | reject_def` lets a blank consist of only `[^b/short-answer/reject]:`, and mdq-py accepts it. The fill-in text says the blank has the blocks of a short answer question and that it carries the rules of short answer (line 465-469), which suggests the accept block is required. No example covers a reject-only blank.
data.impact: One implementation may require the accept block by inheritance, another may not.
data.fix: State whether the accept block is required for a blank, and add an example either way.
data.conditions: A short answer blank defined only by a reject block.

data.title: A blank with an empty accept block does not always leave its responses to the instructor
data.snippet:
`[^slug/short-answer]` block has no pattern has no `accept` list, and the
instructor grades its responses, see [Automation](#automation).
data.description: By short-answer.md (Grading, Automation), a blank with no accept pattern but with a reject block is semi-automatic: the reject patterns settle some responses. With `unmatched: incorrect` in the frontmatter, no response goes to the instructor (and `no-correct-answer` is reported). The sentence says the instructor grades its responses without these conditions.
data.impact: Readers may think reject patterns or `unmatched` have no effect on an empty accept block.
data.fix: Say that the blank has no accept list and that `unmatched` defaults to `manual`, so the instructor grades the responses that no reject pattern settles.
data.conditions: An empty `[^slug/short-answer]:` with a reject block or with `unmatched: incorrect`.

data.title: The two grammar snippets of `patterns` disagree
data.snippet: patterns         : answer | nl pattern_list
data.description: The Blank definitions snippet defines `patterns : answer | nl pattern_list`, while the Short answer blanks snippet (line 291) and short-answer.md define `patterns : content | nl lazy_content | nl pattern_list`. `answer` is not defined here and is the name of the tag rule in numeric.md; the lazy-content alternative after an empty tag is missing.
data.impact: The first snippet rejects valid documents (content on lazy lines after an empty tag) and refers to an unrelated rule.
data.fix: Replace line 197 with `patterns : content | nl lazy_content | nl pattern_list`, as on line 291.

data.title: "A blank the student left empty" is not defined
data.snippet: A blank the student left empty scores 0 under every strategy.
data.description: The spec never says what an empty blank is in the response mapping: an absent key, a `null` value, or (for a short answer blank) `""`. responses.md says `""` and a string of spaces in a short answer blank are graded by the rules of the question and are not a skip. So `""` is a wrong answer that, under `no-mistakes`, gives the question 0, and shows `incorrectFeedback`, while an absent key is "not a mistake" (line 425) and shows nothing. Line 380 also excludes an empty blank from numeric feedback without saying what it is.
data.impact: `no-mistakes` scores and feedback differ between implementations depending on how a UI sends an untouched text input.
data.fix: Define an empty blank as an absent key or a `null` value in the response mapping, and say that `""` in a short answer blank is a graded response, as in responses.md.
data.conditions: Grading under `no-mistakes`, or feedback of a short answer blank, when the student left a text input untouched.

data.title: A choice blank is graded "under the strategy the fill-in question declares", but multiple choice has no `no-mistakes` or `all-or-nothing`
data.snippet:
[multiple choice](multiple-choice.md#grading) question, under the strategy
  the fill-in question declares. It is the only kind of blank that can score
data.description: exam.md (Grading) says a multiple choice question accepts neither `no-mistakes` nor `all-or-nothing` and maps both to `partial`. Under those two fill-in strategies, the rule for an unspecified choice score is therefore not defined by the referenced section. Only the explanation under the example table (line 455-456) implies `partial` scoring.
data.impact: An implementer following the normative bullet has no rule for a choice blank under two of the four strategies.
data.fix: State that a choice blank uses `partial` under `partial`, `no-mistakes` and `all-or-nothing`, and `symmetric` under `symmetric`, as the exam table does.
data.conditions: A fill-in question with a choice blank under `no-mistakes` or `all-or-nothing`.

data.title: The example table claims one set of blank scores for every strategy, but the wrong pick scores differ by strategy
data.snippet:
The "blank scores" column lists what each blank scored on its own, in that
order, and every strategy is computed from those three numbers.
data.description: The column shows `-0.5` for a wrong pick, which line 453-456 says holds only under `symmetric`; under the other three strategies the same pick scores 0. So the other columns are not computed from those three numbers. The `partial` values match only because `partial` also clamps negatives to 0.
data.impact: Readers can conclude that a choice blank scores -0.5 under `partial` and that the clamp in `partial` is what removes it.
data.fix: Say that the column holds the `symmetric` blank scores and that the wrong pick scores 0 under the other strategies, or show both values.

data.title: No grading corpus for fill-in
data.snippet: ## Grading
data.description: examples/grading has corpora for multiple choice, multiple selection, true/false, numeric and short answer, but none for fill-in. No shared test exercises the four combination strategies, the example table, empty blanks, a pending short answer blank making the whole question pending, the feedback order of the flat list (line 384-386), or the automation of a mixed question.
data.impact: mdq-py and mdq-js can diverge on fill-in scores and feedback without any shared test failing.
data.fix: Add examples/grading/fill-in.yaml covering the table rows, empty blanks, pending blanks and feedback order.

data.title: Several parse errors of the blank definitions have no rule in the Additional Rules table
data.snippet: choice or a piece of text, so `[^planet/short-answer(km)]` is not valid syntax.
data.description: The table has one `parse-error` row for blanks (a short answer block defined twice). The corpus expects `parse-error` for cases the table and often the text do not state: an unknown kind suffix (fill-in-unknown-blank-kind), a unit on a short answer tag (fill-in-unit-on-short-answer-tag, line 206 only says "not valid syntax"), two definitions of one choice blank (fill-in-two-choice-definitions), one slug defined with two kinds (fill-in-two-kinds-one-blank), and a blank line between a choice tag and its list (fill-in-blank-line-before-choices, line 226 uses a lowercase "must" and gives no code; the same situation in a short answer blank is only the `detached-answer-list` warning). The prose also never states that blank ids must be unique; only the table row `duplicate-blank-id` and the schema description do.
data.impact: The rules exist only in the corpus; a reader of the spec cannot tell which code to report.
data.fix: State each rule in the text with MUST and add the matching `parse-error` rows, including the choice-blank detached list.

data.title: The JSON `type` of a choice blank is never stated in the spec
data.snippet: ## Multiple choice blanks
data.description: The spec shows the JSON form of short answer and numeric blanks (`type: short-answer`, `type: numeric`) but never says that a choice blank is `type: multiple-choice` in JSON. Only schema/fill-in.yaml (ChoiceBlank) says it. The two-choice minimum is also only in the table, not in the section.
data.impact: Authors of YAML/JSON documents must read the schema to write a choice blank.
data.fix: Add the JSON form of the choice blank of the first example to this section.
data.conditions: Writing a fill-in question in YAML or JSON.

data.title: No example exercises blanks in list items, table cells, blockquotes or a preamble paragraph
data.snippet: At the block level, the hosting block MUST be an ordinary paragraph. Blanks in
data.description: The corpus covers a heading, a link, emphasis, a code span, fenced code and an epilogue paragraph. It has no case for a `[^slug]` in a list item, a table cell, a blockquote (blockquote-preamble has none inside the quote), or an ordinary preamble paragraph (line 178-180).
data.impact: These MUST rules are not checked by the shared tests.
data.fix: Add valid or invalid examples for each block kind once the behavior is settled.

data.title: Blank description says a bare tag infers its kind from the definition that follows
data.snippet: (`[^capital]:` infers its kind from the definition that follows,
data.description: fill-in.md line 203-204 says a bare `[^slug]:` is a choice blank: the kind comes from the tag, not from the content. A bare tag followed by a pattern is not a short answer blank.
data.impact: Misleads readers of the schema into writing `[^x]: Brasília` for a short answer blank.
data.fix: Say that a bare `[^capital]:` is a choice blank, while `[^size/numeric]:` and `[^x/short-answer]:` state their kind.

data.title: ShortAnswerBlank descriptions are stale
data.snippet: machinery: a list of accepted responses, a regular expression, or
data.description: The blank has `accept`/`reject` pattern lists only; a regex is one kind of pattern, not an alternative to the lists. The `accept` description says the `[^id/short-answer/accept]` block sets it, citing only the alias and not the main spelling `[^id/short-answer]`.
data.impact: Minor confusion about the blank's fields.
data.fix: Describe the blank as having `accept` and `reject` pattern lists; cite `[^id/short-answer]` (alias `[^id/short-answer/accept]`).

data.title: `grading` description omits the per-type entry of an exam grading map
data.snippet: `inherit`, the default, takes the exam's `grading` value, and
data.description: fill-in.md line 398-399 says `inherit` takes the exam's `grading`, or its `fill-in` entry when the exam's `grading` is a map, through the exam translation table.
data.impact: Minor.
data.fix: Mention the `fill-in` entry of a grading map.

data.title: `unmatched` description drops the per-blank default
data.snippet: Applies to every short answer blank of the question, with the
data.description: The local description replaces the one of short-answer.yaml#/$defs/unmatched, and does not say that, when absent, each blank takes `incorrect` if it has an accept pattern and `manual` otherwise (fill-in.md footnote 6, line 47-50).
data.impact: Readers may assume a single question-level default.
data.fix: Add: if absent, each blank takes its own default, `incorrect` with an accept pattern and `manual` without one.

data.title: fill-in.md has two different `patterns` rules
data.snippet: patterns         : answer | nl pattern_list
data.description: The Blank definitions section declares `patterns : answer | nl pattern_list`, while the Short answer blanks section (fill-in.md:291) and short-answer.md:150 declare `patterns : content | nl lazy_content | nl pattern_list`. `answer` is not defined in fill-in.md; the only `answer` rule of the spec is the numeric tag (numeric.md:75). Counter-example: `[^capital/short-answer]:` followed by a line `Brasília` is valid by fill-in.md:291 and by the text at fill-in.md:317-319 (a lazy line continues the content after an empty tag), but the rule at line 197 has no `nl lazy_content` branch and rejects it. If `answer` resolves to numeric.md, `[^x/short-answer]: [numeric]: 42` matches the line-197 rule.
data.impact: Two copies of the same rule in one document disagree, and one refers to an unrelated rule. A reader or a grammar tool that takes the first copy gets a different language.
data.fix: Replace line 197 with the rule at line 291: `patterns : content | nl lazy_content | nl pattern_list`.

data.title: Stem rule allows only one inline element between blanks
data.snippet: stem  : inline_md? (blank inline_md?)+
data.description: `inline_md` is defined as 'any valid inline markdown element' (singular, fill-in.md:145), and the rule allows at most one of them before, between and after blanks. Counter-example: the stem `The **capital** of Brazil is [^capital].` has three inline elements before the blank (text, strong, text). The text at fill-in.md:152-176 allows markup elsewhere in the paragraph as long as the blank itself is in a plain-text run, so this stem is valid, but the rule rejects it (tested with Lark, `inline_md` stubbed as TEXT | STRONG | LINK).
data.impact: The grammar rejects ordinary stems with any formatting, or the reader must guess that `inline_md` means a sequence.
data.fix: Use `inline_md*` in the rule, or say that `inline_md` is a sequence of inline elements.

data.title: `blank` matches the text of a link `[^x](url)`
data.snippet: blank : "[^" SLUG "]"
data.description: `CHOICE_ID`, `CHOICE_MARK` and `VALUE_END` exclude a `]` followed by `(` or `[` because that bracket starts a markdown link. `blank` has no such lookahead. Counter-example: in the stem `Veja [^nota](https://www.ibge.gov.br) agora.`, CommonMark (and markdown-it, where the footnote reference rule runs after `link`) reads a link with the text `^nota`. The stem rule reads the blank `nota` followed by the text `(https://www.ibge.gov.br) agora.` (tested with Lark: the only parse is blank + text). The same holds for `[^nota][ref]`.
data.impact: The grammar and the markdown parser disagree on whether the stem has a blank, so an implementation that follows the grammar reports `undefined-blank` for a valid link.
data.fix: Add the lookahead of `CHOICE_ID` to the rule (`"]"` not followed by `(` or `[`), and say in the text that `[^x](url)` and `[^x][ref]` are links.

data.title: Split reading of `**start [^blank] end**` is legal under the stem rule
data.snippet:
interpreted as an unclosed bold element `**start `, followed by a blank and then
the text ` end**`. In both approaches, the result would be illegal according to
the spec, so both parsing strategies are valid.
data.description: The text says that splitting the paragraph around the blank also gives an illegal stem. It does not: CommonMark reads `**start ` alone as the literal text `**start ` (an unmatched delimiter run is text), so the split gives text, blank, text, which `stem : inline_md? (blank inline_md?)+` accepts. Only the whole-paragraph reading (a strong element that contains a blank) is illegal. The corpus (examples/invalid/fill-in-misplaced-blank-emphasis) expects `misplaced-blank`, so an implementation that uses the split strategy, which the text allows, accepts a document the corpus rejects.
data.impact: The text allows a parsing strategy that gives a different result from the corpus.
data.fix: Require the markdown inline parse of the whole paragraph first, and state that a blank inside any inline element is `misplaced-blank`. Remove the claim that both strategies agree.

data.title: Stem rule is one inline run, but the text puts blanks in blocks of the stem
data.snippet:
illegal. A `[^slug]` found in any of them is not a blank: implementations MUST
either reject the document or leave the text exactly as written, and MUST NOT
data.description: The stem rule describes one paragraph (a run of inline elements). The text then discusses blanks in headings, list items, table cells and block quotes as if they were part of the stem, and lets each implementation choose between rejecting the document (`misplaced-blank`) and leaving the text. It also says (fill-in.md:178-180) that a `[^slug]` in the preamble is literal text with no error. Counter-example: `## A capital do Brasil é [^capital]` followed by the paragraph `Complete a frase do título.` and `[^capital/short-answer]: Brasília`. By the stem rule the heading is preamble, the `[^capital]` is text, and the definition is `unreferenced-blank` (this is what examples/invalid/fill-in-misplaced-blank-heading expects). By lines 155-159 an implementation MAY instead report `misplaced-blank` for the heading.
data.impact: Two conforming implementations give different errors for the same document; the file name of the corpus example and its expected code disagree for the same reason.
data.fix: State that the stem of a fill-in question is one paragraph (the rule at line 141), that every block before it is preamble, and remove the 'MUST either reject or leave' option for blocks outside the stem.

data.title: `[^slug]: text` matches no definition rule
data.snippet:
The suffix `/short-answer` is REQUIRED. Without it the definition is a
[multiple choice blank](#multiple-choice-blanks), which is what a bare
`[^slug]:` introduces.
data.description: `choice_def : ws? "[^" SLUG "]" ws? ":" ws? nl choice_list` requires a line ending right after the colon. Counter-example: `[^capital]: Brasília` (a short answer blank written without the suffix, a likely mistake). It matches no `blank_def` rule (tested with Lark: rejected), but the text says that without the suffix 'the definition is a multiple choice blank'. The line does match the stem rule (blank followed by the text `: Brasília`). The spec does not say if it is a `parse-error`, a malformed choice blank or an epilogue paragraph that leaves `[^capital]` undefined.
data.impact: Implementations can report `parse-error`, `undefined-blank` or treat the line as text for the same document.
data.fix: Say what a line that starts with `[^slug]:` and has text after the colon is, for example a `parse-error` whose message suggests the `/short-answer` suffix, and add a corpus example.

data.title: `pattern_item` includes the list marker, `item` does not
data.snippet: pattern_item : ws? LIST_MARK ws content nl (blank_line* observations)?
data.description: grammar.md:73-75 says the grammar of a list item applies to the content of the item after the removal of the list marker and its padding. The choice `item` of choices.md:66 follows that (it starts with `ws? "["`), but `pattern_item` starts with `ws? LIST_MARK ws`. fill-in.md uses both in the same way (`choice_list : item+`, `pattern_list : pattern_item+`, each 'the unordered list those items form'). Counter-example in Lark: the fill-in example `[^capital]:` + `* [ ] Lisbon` + `* [*] Brasília` is rejected by `choice_list : item+`, while `[ ] Lisbon` without `* ` is accepted; for `pattern_list` it is the reverse. Applied to the content of an item as grammar.md says, `pattern_item` rejects `Jupiter` (the content of `* Jupiter`).
data.impact: The two list rules that fill-in reuses follow opposite conventions; a literal reading of either one rejects the examples of the other.
data.fix: Remove `ws? LIST_MARK ws` from `pattern_item` (the list marker belongs to the list, as for `item`), or add it to `item` and change grammar.md:73-75. Pick one convention for both.

data.title: Two `value` rules collide in a fill-in grammar
data.snippet: with the `value` rule of [multiple choice](multiple-choice.md#body), and
data.description: A choice blank uses the `item` rule with the `value` of multiple-choice.md:46 (`ws | ws? "*" ws? | ws? percent ws?`), and a numeric blank uses `numeric_body`, which uses the `value` of numeric.md:81 (`number | fraction`). A grammar of fill-in built from the referenced rules has two different rules called `value`. To compile the test grammar, the numeric one had to be renamed.
data.impact: The fill-in grammar cannot be assembled from the referenced snippets without renaming a rule.
data.fix: Rename one of the rules, for example `numeric_value` in numeric.md or `choice_value` in the choice types.

data.title: `pattern_list` accepts a change of bullet character
data.snippet: LIST_MARK    : /[*+-]/
data.description: `LIST_MARK` is chosen per item, so `pattern_list : pattern_item+` accepts `* Jupiter` followed by `- Saturn` as one list (tested with Lark: accepted). In CommonMark a change of bullet character starts a new list, so the second item is a second list that follows the first without a blank line. The text says `pattern_list` is 'the unordered list those items form' (fill-in.md:299). The same holds for `choice_list : item+` (fill-in.md:220).
data.impact: Grammar and markdown parse disagree on how many lists the block has; the second list may become epilogue content in an implementation that follows the markdown AST.
data.fix: State that all items use the same bullet character, or say that the grammar reads consecutive lists with different bullets as one list.

data.title: `LAZY_START` ignores setext heading underlines
data.description: One-line content follows the CommonMark paragraph, and a `---` or `===` line (and also a single `-` or `=`) right after a paragraph line is a setext heading underline: the whole paragraph, tag line included, becomes a heading. The terminal reads them differently. Counter-examples (tested with Lark on the fill-in `accept_def`): `[^p/short-answer]: Rio` + `===` is accepted as the pattern `Rio ===`; `[^p/short-answer]: Rio` + `-` is accepted as `Rio -`; `[^p/short-answer]: Rio` + `---` ends the block with a 'thematic break' (grammar.md:163, short-answer.md:284). In CommonMark all three turn the tag line into a heading, so there is no definition. exam.md:146 already describes this setext behavior for `---`.
data.impact: An implementation that follows the grammar and one that follows the markdown AST disagree on whether the definition exists.
data.fix: Add the setext underline (`=+` or `-+` with optional trailing ws) to the exclusions of `LAZY_START`, and say what happens to a tag line that becomes a setext heading (for example a `parse-error`).

data.title: `LAZY_START` rejects lines that CommonMark reads as paragraph continuation
data.snippet: lazy_content : ws? LAZY_TEXT (nl ws? LAZY_TEXT)*
data.description: Counter-examples, each after `[^p/short-answer]: Rio` (tested with Lark on `accept_def`, all rejected): (1) `    > Negro` and a tab followed by `! Negro`: with four columns of indentation the line cannot start a block quote, so CommonMark reads it as paragraph continuation; the grammar excludes `>` after any `ws?` and the text makes it a `parse-error`. (2) `*   ` and `1.  ` (empty list items): an empty list item cannot interrupt a paragraph, so CommonMark continues the paragraph; `LAZY_START` excludes `[*+-][ \t]` and `1[.)][ \t]` even when only ws follows. (3) A line that starts with a backtick fence whose info string has a backtick, such as `` ```b` ``, is not a fenced code block in CommonMark but `LAZY_START` excludes it.
data.impact: Contrived inputs parse differently in the grammar and in CommonMark.
data.fix: Limit the `>`/`!` exclusion to at most three columns of indentation, exclude list markers only when non-blank text follows, and exclude a backtick fence only when its info string has no backtick.

data.title: `exact` rejects a code span that opens at the end of a line
data.snippet: exact        : FENCE EXACT_TEXT (nl ws? LAZY_EXACT_TEXT)* FENCE ws?
data.description: The exact literal follows the CommonMark code span, where a line ending can follow the opening run. `EXACT_TEXT` is `+`, so the first line must have text after the fence. Counter-example: `[^p/short-answer]:` followed by a single backtick, then the line `Rio Negro` followed by a backtick. The lines join to a backtick, ` Rio Negro` and a backtick: a complete exact literal by the text of short-answer.md:235-239, but the grammar rejects it (tested with Lark). A `schema-error` would be reported for a document that the text accepts.
data.impact: Minimal; authors rarely break a literal right after the fence.
data.fix: Make the text on the first line optional (`EXACT_TEXT?`), or state that the opening run must be followed by text on the same line.

data.text: The NumericBlank `answer` and `unit` patterns of schema/fill-in.yaml match the numeric grammar (exponent of at most 3 digits, nonzero denominator) and the UNIT terminal of grammar.md, and BlankId matches SLUG.
Every complete Markdown example of fill-in.md (lines 8-19, 249-253, 267-278, 331-342) validates with mdq-py with no warning, and the arithmetic of the grading example table checks out row by row.

The frontmatter maps (preAccept, preReject, incorrectFeedback, domain, decimalPlaces) document their mapping onto blank fields with before/after YAML, and the corpus covers an undefined key and a key on the wrong kind of blank.

data.description: The corpus gives `parse-error` for cases the Additional Rules table does not list and the text does not settle: a blank line between `[^bioma]:` and its choice list (`examples/invalid/fill-in-blank-line-before-choices`; line 226 says 'must start on the following line' but gives no code), an unknown kind suffix such as `[^resposta/essay]:` (`fill-in-unknown-blank-kind`), a unit on a short answer tag (`fill-in-unit-on-short-answer-tag`; line 206 only says 'not valid syntax'), two choice definitions for one id (`fill-in-two-choice-definitions`) and one id with two kinds (`fill-in-two-kinds-one-blank`). Text on the tag line of a choice definition (`[^capital]: Brasília`) has no stated outcome. The table also omits the rule of line 319-321 that a list item right after the content of a short answer definition is a `parse-error`; the short answer table has it (`docs/question-types/short-answer.md:511`).
data.fix: State each rule in the text with MUST and add a `parse-error` row per case: blank line before the choice list, text on a choice tag line, unknown kind suffix, unit on a non-numeric tag, a second definition of an id (any kind), and a list item right after short answer content.

data.description: A choice blank uses the `item` rule with the `value` of multiple-choice.md:46 (`ws | ws? "*" ws? | ws? percent ws?`), and a numeric blank uses `numeric_body`, which uses the `value` of numeric.md:79 (`number | fraction`). A grammar of fill-in built from the referenced rules has two different rules called `value`. To compile the test grammar, the numeric one had to be renamed.

data.text: `numeric_def` holds, and its two copies in fill-in.md are identical and match the numeric `answer` tag. Tested with Lark: accepted `[^size/numeric]: 2750000 +- 10%`, `[^size/numeric]:42`, `[^length/numeric(km)]: 6400 +- 5%`, `[^x/numeric(m/s)]: 1`, `-1/3`, `6.022e23 +- 0.001e23`, `3.14 +- 5% +- 0.1`, `3.14+-0.1`, `1e05`; rejected `1/0`, `1e3/2`, `1e1000`, `01`, `3,14`, `1 000`, `3.14 ± 0.1`, an empty body, `[^x/numeric (km)]`, `[^x/numeric()]`, `[^x/numeric/accept]`, `[^x/Numeric]`.

`accept_def` and `reject_def` hold, their two copies in fill-in.md are identical, and they match `accept_block`/`reject_block` of short-answer.md with the `[^SLUG` prefix. Tested with Lark: accepted single-line literal, exact (`` `` `date` `` ``), regex (`/a/b/`, `/[Bb]ras[íi]lia/i`), multi-line inexact, exact and regex content, lazy content after an empty tag, an empty accept tag, the `/accept` alias and list forms with feedback, comment and lazy lines; rejected an empty reject tag, `[^planet/short-answer(km)]`, `/short-answer/accept/reject`, an unknown kind (`/essay`), `/usr` (unclosed regex), `` `math.isnan` (x) ``, a `>` line after content or after an empty tag, a list after a blank line, and a list right after content.

`choice_def` holds and its two copies are equivalent (`"[^" SLUG "]"` and `blank`). With list-item content as grammar.md defines it, Lark accepted the choice-blank-rich items (`[*] [andes] ...` with feedback and comment, `[50%]`, `[-25%]`), `[^capital]:` with trailing ws and up to 3 spaces of indentation; it rejected a blank line before the list, text after the colon followed by a list, and the multiple-selection value `[x]`.

The stem rule accepts the stems of the corpus: two blanks in one sentence, a stem that starts with a blank, and blanks separated by plain text; it rejects a stem without a blank, in line with the `blanks` minimum of one.

The stem of a fill-in question has no stated limits: which paragraphs form it, which blocks and inline elements may hold a blank, and which code each wrong place gives are settled only by the corpus and by the reference implementation.

Several fill-in rules exist only in the corpus (parse errors of blank definitions) or only in prose with two allowed behaviors, so a second implementation that follows the text can disagree with mdq-py.
No grading corpus exercises fill-in, so the four strategies, empty blanks and pending blanks can drift between mdq-py and mdq-js.

data.title: [Spec] Define the fill-in stem and where a blank may appear
data.summary: The spec does not say which paragraphs form the stem, and allows two behaviors for a `[^slug]` in the wrong place. Options: (a) the stem is the last paragraph before the definitions; a `[^slug]` in an earlier paragraph is an error with a clear message. (b) The stem is every block from the first paragraph with a blank up to the definitions; blanks may appear in several paragraphs. Recommended: (b), since cloze texts often span paragraphs. In both cases, give one outcome per context: code (fenced, indented, code span) is literal text; a heading, list item, table cell, blockquote, emphasis or link text of the stem gives `misplaced-blank`; the inline parse of the whole paragraph comes first; `[^x](url)` and `[^x][ref]` are links.
acceptance: The spec states which blocks form the stem
Each context of a `[^slug]` has one outcome and one code
The corpus has a case for a list item, a table cell, a blockquote and a multi-paragraph stem

data.title: [Spec] State the parse rules of the blank definitions
data.summary: State that the definitions form one sequence of blocks, that a stem references each id at most once (or that repeated references share one input), and give a `parse-error` rule for each malformed definition: blank line before the choice list, text on a choice tag line (with a hint to use `/short-answer`), unknown kind suffix, unit on a non-numeric tag, a second definition of an id, and a list item right after short answer content.
acceptance: Each corpus case of a malformed definition has a row in the Additional Rules table
The spec says whether a paragraph may separate two definitions
The spec has a rule for a repeated `[^id]` in the stem

data.title: [Spec] Map the fill-in strategy to the choice blank strategy
data.summary: A choice blank is graded 'under the strategy the fill-in question declares', but multiple choice has no `no-mistakes` or `all-or-nothing`. Recommended: use the exam table (`partial`, `no-mistakes`, `all-or-nothing` give multiple choice `partial`; `symmetric` gives `symmetric`), and say that the example column holds the `symmetric` blank scores.
acceptance: fill-in.md maps each strategy to a multiple choice strategy
The example table says which strategy the blank scores column uses

data.title: [Spec] Define the empty blank and the pending fill-in response
data.summary: State in docs/responses.md that a missing key and `null` are an empty blank, that `{}` is a response with every blank empty (not a skip), and that a value of the wrong type is malformed by the rule of the blank type. State that the instructor scores each pending blank in [0, 1] and the strategy combines the scores. Add examples/grading/fill-in.yaml.
acceptance: The pending rule says what the instructor scores
examples/grading/fill-in.yaml covers the example table, empty blanks, pending blanks and feedback order

data.title: [Spec] Settle the accept block of a short answer blank
data.summary: A short answer question MUST have an accept block, but a blank can have only a reject block. Options: (a) require `[^id/short-answer]` for every short answer blank; (b) allow a reject-only blank and say so. Recommended: (a), the same rule as the question. Also reword line 314-315: without accept patterns, `unmatched` defaults to `manual`, so the instructor grades what no reject pattern settles.
acceptance: fill-in.md says whether a reject-only blank is valid, with a corpus example

data.title: [Spec] Make the list grammars follow one convention
data.summary: `pattern_item` includes the list marker while the choice `item` does not; two `value` rules collide in a fill-in grammar; a change of bullet character is read as one list. Recommended: drop the marker from `pattern_item` (grammar.md:73-75 already says the item grammar applies after the marker), rename the numeric `value` to `numeric_value`, and state that a change of bullet starts a new list.
acceptance: No two rules referenced by fill-in share a name
The spec says what a change of bullet character does

data.title: [Spec] Align lazy lines and exact literals with CommonMark
data.summary: `LAZY_START` ignores setext underlines, excludes some lines that CommonMark continues (indented `>`, empty list items, backtick lines with a backtick in the info string), and `exact` needs text after the opening backticks on the first line. Recommended: follow CommonMark in each case, and state that a tag line that becomes a setext heading is a `parse-error`.
acceptance: The counter-examples of F41 parse as continuation
An exact literal can open at the end of a line

data.text: Define the fill-in stem: which blocks form it and the outcome of a `[^slug]` in each context.
Define the empty blank and the pending fill-in response, and add a fill-in grading corpus.
Map each fill-in strategy to a multiple choice strategy for choice blanks.
Move every parse error of blank definitions from the corpus into the Additional Rules table.
Settle the accept block of a short answer blank.
Align the shared list, lazy line and exact literal grammars with CommonMark and with each other.
Apply the mechanical fixes: grammar copies, schema descriptions and the choice blank term.
